item.content:encoded:
Juan Soto has joined one of the most impressive four-player clubs in the history of Major League Baseball.
Sure, the New York Mets are mired in the midst of a brutally disappointing season, but that didn't stop Soto from a cool accomplishment on Friday night.
The starting point for the feat was this: Soto launched the 270th home run of his MLB career, a 428-foot blast against the Philadelphia Phillies:
It's a cooler feat than just 270 homers, though.
Juan Soto's New History
Soto has become just the fourth player in major league history with at least 270 home runs and at least 100 stolen bases before turning 28 years old, according to MLB's Sarah Langs.
The other three players on the list:
- Ken Griffey Jr.
No old-timers on the list, but those might be the three best pure baseball players of the last few decades, along with Barry Bonds.
A-Rod, Junior and Trout don't need full names to even be identified.
Soto doesn't quite have that going, although if you start talking about a ballplayer named Soto, people will know who you're referring to.
He's not going to have a postseason audience this season, either. A year ago, the Mets collapsed down the stretch. This season, they were never really in the race.
Soto has had a solid season when healthy — in 103 games, he had 26 home runs and a .920 OPS.
Juan Soto Career Stats
Soto has now played in 1,199 MLB games to reach the 270 home run mark.
He also has 210 doubles as part of 1,187 hits and counting.
Soto has also stolen 104 bases in 134 attempts. The big steals year came last season, when he swiped 38 bags pretty much out of nowhere. His previous career-high had been 12 steals in two separate seasons. In 2026, Soto is 9-for-12 stealing bases.
The lefty Soto is also well-known for his ability to work a walk, and it's pretty much historic. He has led all of MLB in walks in four separate seasons, and he has six years with at least 100 walks.
For his career, Soto has walked 969 times and only struck out 893 times, a feat pretty much no one else these days even comes close to.
Soto is the active leader among MLB players in on-base percentage at .415.
He still has a long time to go on his Mets contract, and it's safe to expect Soto to continue adding to his great statistics en route to what very well could be a Hall of Fame career.
At some point, though, Mets fans are going to want to see Soto's production be a part of a playoff team — that was the plan all along when Steven Cohen started dishing out so much money, and it'll be up to Soto in part to lead a turnaround and make things right again at Citi Field.

Soto went 3-for-5 with a double and a three-run home run during the Mets' 6-3 win over the Phillies on Friday.
With the game tied 3-3 in the sixth, Soto doubled the Mets' run total after belting a 428-foot, three-run home run to center field off Orion Kerkering. Given the time he missed this season due to two stints on the IL, the superstar outfielder would need a major power surge over the final week of the regular season in order to reach the 30-homer mark for a fourth consecutive year.

item.content:encoded:
NEW YORK (AP) — Juan Soto hit a three-run homer and the New York Mets kept the Philadelphia Phillies from gaining ground in the National League wild-card race with a 6-3 victory Friday night.
Edmundo Sosa went 3 for 3 with a home run and a double for the Phillies (85-69), who remained tied with the Cubs for the top two wild-card spots after Chicago lost 6-4 to Cincinnati. Both teams began the day one game ahead of the San Diego Padres, who were scheduled to host Miami later Friday.
Derek Hill also went deep and Bryson Stott had an RBI double for Philadelphia.
Soto also doubled and finished with three hits. A.J. Ewing’s two-run single capped a three-run first inning for the last-place Mets, who ended a five-game losing streak — their longest under interim manager Andy Green. Carson Benge had an RBI single in the first and reached base three times.
Francisco Lindor remained at 299 career homers after going 2 for 5 with a double.
Rookie left-hander Zac Thornton (5-5) allowed two runs and five hits in six innings. He struck out four and walked one. Thornton has permitted two runs or fewer eight times in 14 big league starts.
Dedniel Núñez got four outs for his second career save and first since July 13, 2024.
José Urquidy tossed 4 2/3 innings of scoreless bulk relief in his Phillies debut. Urquidy, designated for assignment by the Chicago White Sox on Tuesday, was claimed off waivers Thursday.
Phillies opener Tim Mayza (3-4) was charged with three runs. He threw 33 pitches but recorded just one out — the shortest outing by a Philadelphia starter since Cristopher Sánchez got only one out against the Washington Nationals on July 29, 2021.
Up next
The Mets will retire the No. 15 jersey worn by Hall of Fame center fielder Carlos Beltrán on Saturday before RHP Christian Scott (4-5, 3.76 ERA) opposes Phillies RHP Andrew Painter (3-9, 5.54).

item.content:encoded:
The Mets (70-84) defeated the Philadelphia Phillies (85-69) by a score of 6-3.
Here are the takeaways...
-- Mets left-handed starter Zac Thornton plunked leadoff batter Kyle Schwarber on a 3-2 count to get the game started. The rookie battled back, striking out Trea Turner and Bryce Harper before Mets first baseman Brett Baty made a diving stop on a Luis Arraez grounder down the line to put away the third out.
-- Southpaw Tim Mayza served as the bullpen opener for Philadelphia, and Francisco Lindor jumped all over him with a leadoff double. With one out, Bo Bichette worked a 10-pitch at-bat, culminating in a single to center field which moved Lindor up to third base. Carson Benge kept the line moving and drove in Lindor with an opposite-field single. Mark Vientos was walked to load the bases, and Phillies manager Don Mattingly pulled Mayza for right-handed reliever Jose Urquidy. A.J. Ewing roped an Urquidy fastball for a double, which scored two runs. Urquidy retired the next two Mets batters to limit the damage to three runs.
-- In the second inning, Ewing got turned around on a deep line drive to center, failing to haul in the RBI double for Bryson Stott, which cut the Mets' lead to 3-1. In the bottom half of the inning, Juan Soto doubled into the left-center field gap with two outs, but Urquidy struck out Bichette to end the threat.
-- With two outs away in the top of the sixth, Phillies left fielder Edmundo Sosa blasted a solo shot to left field, his third hit of the night. Excluding Sosa, Thornton allowed just two hits. He struck out four and walked one, allowing two earned runs across 87 pitches.
-- Soto took a hanging breaking ball thrown by Phillies right-hander Orion Kerkering 428 feet for a two-out three-run homer in the bottom of the sixth. Soto's 26th tater of 2026 put the Mets up 6-2.
-- Philadelphia center fielder Derek Hill responded with a solo home run off of Mets left-handed reliever Nate Lavender in the top of the seventh. Lavender persevered, retiring each of the next four batters he faced, before handing the ball to Dedniel Núñez to record the third out of the eighth. In the bottom half of the frame, Bichette grounded into a double play with the bases loaded. Núñez handled the ninth inning and retired the side to earn the first save of his season - and second save of his career - to seal the 6-3 win for the Mets.
Game MVP: Juan Soto
Soto notched his third game with multiple extra-base hits in September, going 3-for-5 with a double and a three-run homer. It was also Soto's third game of the season with at least three hits.
Highlights
What's next
The Mets play the Phillies in the third game of the four-game home series on Saturday at 4:10 p.m. on SNY. They will honor 2026 Baseball Hall of Fame inductee Carlos Beltrán.
New York will send out Christian Scott (3.76 ERA, 1.26 WHIP in 105.1 IP).
Philadelphia is set to start fellow right-hander Andrew Painter (5.54 ERA, 1.44 WHIP in 115.1 IP).
